result.summary: This Outsourcing Agreement governs the licensing and support of E.piphany software applications and professional services for High Speed Net Solutions, Inc. (HSNS). The contract presents notable risks due to one-sided indemnification obligations imposed on HSNS, an absence of mutual liability caps favoring the vendor, and a lack of termination for convenience provisions. Furthermore, data privacy and breach notification terms are completely unaddressed in the provided excerpts.

categoryScores.comment: R-B-INDEM-01 Fail: The contract imposes a heavy, one-sided indemnification obligation on HSNS while E.piphany's IP indemnity is severely limited and excludes mutual protections for data or gross negligence.
R-B-LIAB-01 Fail: Liability is capped unilaterally based on total payments made under the initial term without mutual caps or standard super-caps for confidentiality breaches.
R-B-TERM-01 Partial: The contract provides a standard 30-day cure period for material breaches, but it lacks any provision for termination for convenience.
R-B-PRIV-01 Not Addressed: The provided contract excerpts are completely silent regarding data privacy standards, SOC 2 compliance, and security incident notification timeframes.
R-B-PAY-01 Not Addressed: Specific invoice payment terms (such as Net 30) are not detailed in the provided excerpts, as fees are referenced across exhibits.

keyFacts.label: Liability Cap
keyFacts.value: Sum total of payments made by HSNS under the initial term

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Protects vendor interests by maintaining asymmetric liability limits and broad customer indemnities.
keyPoints: Retain the unilateral limitation of liability capped at initial term payments.
Ensure HSNS holds E.piphany harmless for outsourcing operations and third-party claims.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Resist mutualizing indemnification obligations and maintain strict exclusions of consequential damages.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Focuses on closing the transaction while ensuring operational continuity and realistic milestones.
keyPoints: Secure clear acceptance testing and professional services standards.
Ensure post-termination transition rights for outsourcing customers are preserved.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Accept current payment structures but push for a termination for convenience clause to maintain business flexibility.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Evaluates agreement against playbook tolerances to mitigate severe legal and financial exposures.
keyPoints: Rule R-B-INDEM-01 fails due to unreciprocated customer indemnification.
Rule R-B-LIAB-01 fails due to lack of mutual liability and confidentiality super-caps.
Rule R-B-PRIV-01 is entirely missing data privacy and security incident terms.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Require mutual indemnity, a 12-month fee liability cap with super-caps, and a comprehensive data privacy addendum.

redlines.originalText:
HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers,

directors and partners (each, an "Indemnified Party") against any and all claims, demands, causes of action, damages, costs, expenses, penalties, losses and liabilities
redlines.proposedText: Each party shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other party and its officers, directors and partners against any and all claims, demands, causes of action, damages, costs, expenses, penalties, losses and liabilities arising out of or resulting from its material breach of this Agreement or third-party IP infringement.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany will argue that as the core technology provider, they bear disproportionate risks requiring broad indemnification from partners.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Unilateral indemnification exposes HSNS to unlimited third-party liabilities without reciprocal protections.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: A balanced market standard requires mutual indemnification for third-party claims and material breaches.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We can agree to protect E.piphany against IP claims related to our services, but we require mutual indemnification for general breach. Fallback: mutual IP and breach indemnification.

redlines.originalText: This Agreement shall continue for a term set forth in Exhibit B, and may be renewed for successive one (1) year terms pursuant to mutual written agreement of the parties, unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Section 12.1.
redlines.proposedText: This Agreement shall continue for a term set forth in Exhibit B, and may be terminated by either party for convenience upon sixty (60) days prior written notice, or earlier pursuant to this Section 12.1.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany will insist on term certainty to ensure return on investment for their deployed technology and predictable revenue.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Locking into a multi-year term without a convenience exit creates severe commercial rigidity if business needs change.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Standard tech contracts include a termination for convenience clause with adequate notice to allow orderly wind-down.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: A 60-day notice for termination for convenience provides adequate predictability while avoiding perpetual lock-in. Fallback: 90 days notice.

redlines.originalText: The parties agree to hold each other's Confidential Information in confidence for a period of five (5) years after disclosure of the Confidential Information or for a period of two (2) years after termination of this Agreement, whichever is earlier.
redlines.proposedText: The parties agree to hold each other's Confidential Information in confidence for a period of five (5) years after disclosure of the Confidential Information.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: Counsel may prefer complex termination-linked survival periods to shorten confidentiality burdens.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Tying confidentiality to termination terms creates ambiguity regarding long-term sensitive data protection.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: A standard fixed 5-year post-disclosure survival period ensures clear, predictable protection for proprietary information.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: Simplifying to a straight 5-year post-disclosure period removes ambiguity. Fallback: accept 3 years for non-trade secret info.

redlines.originalText: A party's failure to respond to the submission of material for approval with any recommended changes within three (3) business days shall be deemed an approval of the submission.
redlines.proposedText: A party's failure to respond to the submission of material for approval with any recommended changes within ten (10) business days shall be deemed an approval of the submission.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: E.piphany wants rapid turnaround to keep project implementation schedules moving quickly.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: A three-day window is operationally unfeasible and risks accidental approval of critical deliverables due to brief review times.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Extending the review period to ten business days provides a commercially reasonable window for adequate legal and technical review.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: Three days is too tight for proper review cycles; ten days aligns with standard commercial practices. Fallback: five business days.

obligations.requirement: HSNS shall meet with E.piphany on a quarterly basis to discuss non-binding forecasts and provide a non-binding, rolling six-month forecast report.
obligations.breachConsequence: Material breach if uncured after notice

obligations.requirement: HSNS shall pay all amounts due and owing within thirty days from the date of E.piphany's invoice.
obligations.breachConsequence: Overdue payments shall accrue a late payment charge at the lesser of one and one half percent per month or maximum rate allowed under law.

obligations.requirement: HSNS shall not remove any E.piphany trademark, copyright or other proprietary notices and shall reproduce such notices on copies.
Upon termination, HSNS shall discontinue use of the Application and certify in writing that all copies have been returned or destroyed.
Hold each other's Confidential Information in confidence for the specified retention period.
obligations.triggerOrDeadline: Five years after disclosure or two years after termination, whichever is earlier

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers, directors and partners (each, an Indemnified Party) against any and all claims, demands, causes of action, damages, costs, expenses, penalties, losses and liabilities incurred or to be incurred by an Indemnified Party.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Indemnification — Market Mutual IP & Third-Party Indemnification
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Provider Indemnification. Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer... (b) Customer Indemnification. Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Provider... (c) Procedure. The indemnified party shall provide prompt written notice...
deviations: The contract lacks reciprocal indemnification from the Provider for third-party IP infringement.
missingProtections: Provider IP indemnification and claim defense procedures.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Add mutual intellectual property indemnification protections to safeguard the customer from infringement claims.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: 3.1, 3.4, 4.3, 6.2, 6.4, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13 and 14 shall survive any termination or expiration of this Agreement. All other rights and licenses granted herein will cease upon termination.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Provisions which by their nature should survive termination, including confidentiality, indemnification, limitation of liability, payment of accrued fees, data return and deletion, and governing law, survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement.
deviations: Uses a specific list of section numbers instead of a general standard definition for surviving clauses.
missingProtections: Explicit enumeration of all standard surviving provisions by nature.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Ensure all critical clauses such as confidentiality and indemnification are explicitly captured in the survival list.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: THIS ALLOCATION TO WHICH THE PARTIES HAVE AGREED. THIS LIMITATION OF LIABILITY APPLIES NOTWITHSTANDING ANY FAILURE OF THE ESSENTIAL PURPOSE OF THE EXCLUSIVE REMEDIES.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Limitation of Liability — 12-Month Trailing Aggregate Fee Cap with Balanced Super-Cap
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Consequential Damages Waiver. Except for breaches of Section 7... (b) General Aggregate Cap... (c) Super-Cap for Data Protection Breaches...
deviations: The excerpt primarily highlights the failure of essential purpose disclaimer without detailing specific caps.
missingProtections: Twelve-month trailing aggregate fee cap and super-caps for data breaches.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Incorporate a standard aggregate fee cap and explicit consequential damages waivers.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS acknowledges that E.piphany retains all right, title and interest in the Application and any modifications thereto... HSNS hereby assigns all right, title and interest in and to any customization, enhancement, amendment or changes made by or for HSNS.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: IP Rights — Customer Work Product Ownership & Non-Use of Customer Data for AI Training
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Work Product. All custom deliverables... belong exclusively to Customer upon payment. (b) Customer Data & AI Model Boundaries. Customer retains all right... Provider shall not use Customer Data... to train... any generalized artificial intelligence...
deviations: Customizations and modifications are assigned to Provider rather than owned by Customer as work for hire.
missingProtections: Customer ownership of custom work product and restrictions on AI training using Customer Data.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Revise IP assignment to ensure Customer owns bespoke deliverables and restricts use of its data for model training.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: For any breach of the warranties contained in Section 4.1, HSNS's sole and exclusive remedy... shall be: (i) in the case of a nonconforming Application, to correct the nonconforming Application... or terminate the Application license and recover the fees paid.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Warranties — Performance Warranty with Re-Performance Remedy
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: The Provider warrants that (a) the Services will perform materially in accordance with the Documentation... If a warranty is breached... Provider shall re-perform or correct the non-conformity...
deviations: Remedies are framed around correction or license termination rather than a standardized re-performance workflow.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Align warranty remedies with industry standards ensuring clear timelines for correction or re-performance.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: HSNS acknowledges that E.piphany retains all right, title and interest in the Application and any modifications thereto... HSNS hereby assigns all right, title and interest in and to any customization, enhancement, amendment or changes made by or for HSNS.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: IP Ownership — Each Party Keeps Its Pre-Existing IP; Licence to Deliverables
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Each party retains all rights in its intellectual property existing before or developed independently of this Agreement. The Customer owns all deliverables created specifically for it upon payment.
deviations: Deliverables and modifications created by Customer are assigned to Provider instead of Customer retaining work product.
missingProtections: Customer retention of custom deliverables and explicit pre-existing IP reservations for Customer.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Clarify that each party retains pre-existing IP and ensure Customer receives ownership of custom deliverables.

rules.ruleTitle: Mutual Indemnity for IP & Gross Negligence
rules.evidence: HSNS hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless E.piphany, and its officers, directors and partners
rules.explanation: The contract imposes a heavy, one-sided indemnification obligation on HSNS while E.piphany's IP indemnity is severely limited and excludes mutual protections for data or gross negligence.
rules.recommendation: Negotiate mutual indemnification provisions, ensuring E.piphany indemnifies HSNS for IP infringement and gross negligence, and limit HSNS's indemnity obligations.

rules.evidence: IN NO EVENT SHALL E.PIPHANY'S LIABILITY HEREUNDER EXCEED THE SUM TOTAL OF PAYMENTS MADE BY HSNS UNDER THE INITIAL TERM OF THIS AGREEMENT.
rules.explanation: Liability is capped unilaterally based on total payments made under the initial term without mutual caps or standard super-caps for confidentiality breaches.
rules.recommendation: Establish a mutual liability cap linked to fees paid over a 12-month period and negotiate a super-cap for confidentiality and data protection breaches.

rules.evidence: either party may terminate this Agreement if the other party... fails to cure a material breach of any term or condition of this Agreement within thirty (30) days
rules.explanation: The contract provides a standard 30-day cure period for material breaches, but it lacks any provision for termination for convenience.
rules.recommendation: Add a termination for convenience clause allowing either party to terminate upon 60 days prior written notice.

rules.explanation: The provided contract excerpts are completely silent regarding data privacy standards, SOC 2 compliance, and security incident notification timeframes.
rules.recommendation: Incorporate a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) requiring 48-hour security incident notification and annual SOC 2 Type II audit reports upon request.

rules.explanation: Specific invoice payment terms (such as Net 30) are not detailed in the provided excerpts, as fees are referenced across exhibits.
rules.recommendation: Explicitly define standard Net 30 payment terms and good-faith dispute procedures in the payment section.

opposingFindings.issue: The indemnification obligation is entirely one-sided, requiring HSNS to indemnify E.piphany without reciprocal protections for HSNS.

opposingFindings.quote: Upon prior written notice, either party may terminate this Agreement if the other party becomes insolvent... or fails to cure a material breach of any term or condition of this Agreement within thirty (30) days
opposingFindings.issue: The agreement lacks any provision allowing for termination for convenience, locking the parties into the contract term.
opposingFindings.leverage: E.piphany will insist on term certainty to ensure return on investment for their deployed technology and predictable revenue.
